{
  "hook": "Les Routes pushes 100% Syrah into Gigondas, defying the appellation's Grenache minimum by sourcing from high-elevation Dentelles slopes where limestone scree forces deep roots. This choice amplifies pepper and mineral notes over fruit density. Critics score it 94-95 points across recent vintages.",
  "wine_summary": "Des Bosquets crafts Les Routes as a single-varietal Syrah from Gigondas, a southern Rhône cru at the Dentelles de Montmirail's base, where reds deliver power at lower prices than Châteauneuf-du-Pape. The domaine follows biodynamic, organic, and vegan practices, emphasizing site-specific expression. Terroir here—stony marl and decomposed limestone—yields wines with density and freshness, and this bottling's all-Syrah focus highlights the grape's savory edge amid Gigondas's typical Grenache dominance.",
  "terroir_expression": "Dentelles slopes deliver thin, rocky limestone marl and scree that retain heat by day but cool via limestone bedrock's mineral influence, distinguishing Gigondas from flatter Rhône zones. These soils drive deep roots in Les Routes' high sites, yielding concentrated blackberry, black pepper from rotundone, and olive tapenade notes with firm tannins and persistent mineral freshness in the glass.",
  "vinification_summary": "2023 saw 18 months in oak, building structure without overwhelming Syrah's savory core; other vintages like 2020 at 14.5% ABV follow suit with minimal intervention. *Élevage* (the aging period post-fermentation) integrates oak tannins with fruit, preserving pepper and meaty character while adding subtle smoke. Biodynamic farming ensures clean fruit for this precise approach.",
  "food_pairing": "Lamb tagine with apricots and ras el hanout—Syrah's black pepper and smoked meat match the spices, while mineral acidity cuts richness. Nashville hot chicken—pepper notes echo the heat, and firm tannins stand up to fried crust. Fine dining: braised short ribs with black olive tapenade—savory olive and leather align with the dish's umami depth. Pork belly bao buns—dark fruit bridges sweet-savory pork, acidity refreshes the fat. Grilled sardines with fennel—violet and mineral lift the fish's brininess.",
  "comparable_wines": "Cornas Syrah from Northern Rhône—similar cool-site pepper and mineral focus, but Les Routes adds Gigondas warmth. Vacqueyras Les Routes by same producer—Grenache blend for comparison, less pepper-driven but same stony soil vibrancy.",
  "style_profile": "Full-bodied Syrah with firm tannins and black pepper thrust",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink 2023-2028 for 2023 vintage; earlier for 2022. Store cool (55°F) and humid (70%) away from light.",
  "value_assessment": "$40-50 retail. Beats Châteauneuf Syrah cuvées at this price like Clos des Papes' seconds. Worth every dollar for 94-point density and ageworthiness.",
  "market_position": "Sommeliers list it for Rhône flights in urban bistros. Retail targets collectors building southern Rhône cellars. Casual enthusiasts grab it for winter roasts.",
  "insider_take": "Skip if you chase Grenache fruit bombs—Les Routes trades plushness for Syrah's meaty tension. Northern Rhône fans will stock it over Barossa Shiraz for restraint. Most miss how Dentelles altitude tempers alcohol into finesse.",

parsed.hook: Les Routes pushes 100% Syrah into Gigondas, defying the appellation's Grenache minimum by sourcing from high-elevation Dentelles slopes where limestone scree forces deep roots. This choice amplifies pepper and mineral notes over fruit density. Critics score it 94-95 points across recent vintages.
parsed.wine_summary: Des Bosquets crafts Les Routes as a single-varietal Syrah from Gigondas, a southern Rhône cru at the Dentelles de Montmirail's base, where reds deliver power at lower prices than Châteauneuf-du-Pape. The domaine follows biodynamic, organic, and vegan practices, emphasizing site-specific expression. Terroir here—stony marl and decomposed limestone—yields wines with density and freshness, and this bottling's all-Syrah focus highlights the grape's savory edge amid Gigondas's typical Grenache dominance.
parsed.terroir_expression: Dentelles slopes deliver thin, rocky limestone marl and scree that retain heat by day but cool via limestone bedrock's mineral influence, distinguishing Gigondas from flatter Rhône zones. These soils drive deep roots in Les Routes' high sites, yielding concentrated blackberry, black pepper from rotundone, and olive tapenade notes with firm tannins and persistent mineral freshness in the glass.
parsed.vinification_summary: 2023 saw 18 months in oak, building structure without overwhelming Syrah's savory core; other vintages like 2020 at 14.5% ABV follow suit with minimal intervention. *Élevage* (the aging period post-fermentation) integrates oak tannins with fruit, preserving pepper and meaty character while adding subtle smoke. Biodynamic farming ensures clean fruit for this precise approach.
parsed.food_pairing: Lamb tagine with apricots and ras el hanout—Syrah's black pepper and smoked meat match the spices, while mineral acidity cuts richness. Nashville hot chicken—pepper notes echo the heat, and firm tannins stand up to fried crust. Fine dining: braised short ribs with black olive tapenade—savory olive and leather align with the dish's umami depth. Pork belly bao buns—dark fruit bridges sweet-savory pork, acidity refreshes the fat. Grilled sardines with fennel—violet and mineral lift the fish's brininess.
parsed.comparable_wines: Cornas Syrah from Northern Rhône—similar cool-site pepper and mineral focus, but Les Routes adds Gigondas warmth. Vacqueyras Les Routes by same producer—Grenache blend for comparison, less pepper-driven but same stony soil vibrancy.

parsed.cellar_recommendation: Drink 2023-2028 for 2023 vintage; earlier for 2022. Store cool (55°F) and humid (70%) away from light.
parsed.value_assessment: $40-50 retail. Beats Châteauneuf Syrah cuvées at this price like Clos des Papes' seconds. Worth every dollar for 94-point density and ageworthiness.
parsed.market_position: Sommeliers list it for Rhône flights in urban bistros. Retail targets collectors building southern Rhône cellars. Casual enthusiasts grab it for winter roasts.
parsed.insider_take: Skip if you chase Grenache fruit bombs—Les Routes trades plushness for Syrah's meaty tension. Northern Rhône fans will stock it over Barossa Shiraz for restraint. Most miss how Dentelles altitude tempers alcohol into finesse.
